setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (2 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Bird Song second favorite of all, behind the Veneta version, though the tape quality is poor; Reviewer singles out the Bird Song as a highlight [4][13]
- **//He's Gone** (2 reviews): Reviewer says the He's Gone jam into Other One is the best such segue ever, a beautiful small jam never matched; Reviewer calls the He's Gone jam pretty good and the Other One typical of the period, meaning excellent [6][8]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Other One hefty and a highlight [13]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Reviewer names the Half Step possibly a personal favorite version [6]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-09-19.154185.aud.deal.smith.clugston.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 166 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: This transfer is described as a marked improvement over previously circulating audience copies [13]
- **gd72-09-19.aud.cotsman.12075.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 141 min; rated 2.56/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Quality is decent for an old outdoor audience tape, but not impressive; reviewer rates sound a C; Reviewer, apparently the taper, laments that no better-sounding tape has surfaced over the years; Reviewer finds the audience recording not the best, but good enough to suggest a strong show [2][4][6][12]
- **gd1972-09-19.152468.s1-s2p.aud.flac2448**: audience recording; 17 songs; 89 min [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; weather was chilly and damp, and sound and equipment problems forced the band to take several short breaks [5]
- A swami demonstrated mind over matter between sets, lying on a bed of nails with cinder blocks on his chest [7]
- New Riders played Death and Destruction, which reviewer believes they did only this once in the 1970s [7]
- New Riders opened on what reviewer recalls as near their last tour with the band; they played Death and Destruction [10]
- Reviewer saw the Riders play Death and Destruction again at a college a couple of months later, calling it rare [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-09-19.154185.aud.deal.smith.clugston.flac16**: taped by Ed Deal; transferred by Matt Smith, Scott Clugston; source: Ed Deal's Master Audience Cassettes (Sony C-90); Unknown equipment [1]. Also: JCotsman's audience source supplies the first twelve seconds of Big Railroad Blues and a seventeen-second patch in Stella Blue [1]
- **gd72-09-19.aud.cotsman.12075.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience [2]. Also: Taper, thought to be Jerry Moore, saved tape by cutting into every song, so a few notes are missing from each; Soundboards reportedly sit in the vault with a missing reel; reviewer guesses which reel is absent; Lineage is audience, to MC, to unknown, to digital, to CD; came via Paul Hartman and was seeded by JCotsman [2][4][12]
- **gd1972-09-19.152468.s1-s2p.aud.flac2448**: taped by from the collection of Rich Petrunis; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 05/2021; source: Unknown mono AU [3]
